content: {"rule":"K-G4","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text counts verses toward a broken link, which is the act K-G4 governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D2 vs C3 (Matthew 1:18, 25): CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 \"before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost\" and Matthew 1:25 \"knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son\" contradict C3's claim of espousal union; [L2] πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν (prin ē synelthein, Strong's G4250/G4905, before coming together) and οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν (ouk eginōsken, Strong's G1097, was not knowing); [L3] Luke 1:34.","rule_words":"A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. A verse the judge says was answered is not counted.","room":"A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way — reading 1: listing verses as support for a broken link counts them, so the quote/name-round requirement applies; reading 2: only an explicit unanswered-witness label counts them.","why":"The judge text lists Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 as support for a broken link but quotes no earlier-round sentence pressing them against that link and names no round, so under K-G4 those verses cannot count as unanswered witnesses."}
